rows.label: Soil liquefaction
rows.learning_takeaway: Explain how shaking can make loose water-saturated sediment lose supporting strength.
rows.card: Strong shaking can make loose, water-saturated sediment lose much of its supporting strength. During soil liquefaction, ground that previously carried buildings or other loads can deform and fail. The hazard depends on the material and water conditions, not just the earthquake’s size.

records.description: geological phenomenon when soil material that is ordinarily a solid behaves like a liquid

rows.label: Standing to sue
rows.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a concrete, redressable legal injury from disagreement with government policy.
rows.card: In US federal court, standing ordinarily requires a concrete, particularized injury that is actual or imminent, linked to the challenged conduct and likely to be redressed by a favorable decision. Disagreeing with a policy is therefore different from showing the personal stake needed to bring the lawsuit.

rows.label: Stereographic projection
rows.learning_takeaway: Project from a sphere’s pole onto a plane to translate spherical locations into planar coordinates.
rows.card: Stereographic projection maps a sphere, apart from its projection pole, onto a plane. Draw a line from the pole through a surface point and continue it to the plane. The construction turns spherical positions into planar coordinates using the geometry of similar triangles.

rows.label: Summary judgment
rows.learning_takeaway: Understand deciding a claim without trial when no material factual dispute requires resolution.
rows.card: In US federal civil procedure, summary judgment can resolve a claim without trial when no genuine dispute of material fact remains and the moving party is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. It does not authorize choosing between competing evidence that a reasonable factfinder could resolve differently.

rows.label: Thrust vectoring
rows.learning_takeaway: Deflect exhaust direction to change a vehicle’s thrust direction and maneuverability.
rows.card: Thrust vectoring redirects an engine’s exhaust so the propulsive force can change direction. This gives a vehicle another way to maneuver rather than keeping thrust along one fixed axis. NASA describes rectangular nozzle exits as one design approach that makes the exhaust flow easier to deflect.

rows.label: Torus
rows.learning_takeaway: Gluing opposite rectangle edges without twists creates a genus-one surface and models two periodic coordinates.
rows.card: An ordinary torus is a surface with one handle, often pictured as a doughnut. It can also be constructed by identifying opposite edges of a rectangle without twists. This edge-gluing description makes the surface useful for representing two independently periodic coordinates.

rows.label: UTF-8
rows.learning_takeaway: Encode Unicode scalar values in one to four bytes while preserving ASCII byte values.
rows.card: UTF-8 represents Unicode scalar values using one to four bytes. ASCII characters retain their familiar single-byte values, while other values use recognizable multibyte patterns. A character's assigned number and its encoded bytes are different things, which matters when counting or processing text.

records.description: variable-width encoding (into one to four bytes) and transformation format of code points for the universal character set defined by ISO/IEC 10646 and The Unicode® Standard, compatible with ASCII

rows.label: XMM-Newton
rows.learning_takeaway: Nested grazing-incidence mirrors focus X-rays while separate instruments collect complementary spectra and optical data.
rows.card: XMM-Newton focuses X-rays with nested mirrors struck at shallow grazing angles. Each of its three mirror modules contains fifty-eight shells, increasing the collecting surface in a compact assembly. Additional instruments separate X-ray wavelengths and observe optical and ultraviolet light, giving complementary information about the same targets.
